newsitem.title: USA: Icahn lifts RJR Nabisco stake, seeks changes.
newsitem.headline: Icahn lifts RJR Nabisco stake, seeks changes.

text.p: Investor Carl Icahn said on Friday he had raised his stake in RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp to 7.3 percent from 5.8 percent and called for a new chief executive officer at the company.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Icahn said his holdings now total 19,929,800 shares.
He repeated his call for RJR Nabisco to spin off Nabisco Holdings Corp and said it would be in the best interests of shareholders if RJR Nabisco sought a new chief executive officer.
Icahn also urged that RJR Nabisco's annual dividend be raised to $2 a share from the current $1.85, and that it be maintained at that level after the spin-off of Nabisco Holdings.
Icahn's latest transactions include the purchase of 3,515,000 RJR Nabisco shares October 10-22 at prices ranging from $26 to $27.875 per share, according to the filing.
Icahn also disclosed that earlier this week, tobacco industry analyst Gary Black agreed to lead a slate of nominees for the RJR Nabisco board and to push for Icahn's proposals for the company.
Icahn said he met with RJR Nabisco CEO Steven Goldstoneon on October 23 to discuss the agreement with Black, of Sanford C. Bernstein & Co.

However, on October 24 Black informed Icahn that he had changed his mind and did not wish to lead the Icahn slate although he still favored the investor's proposals for the company, according to the filing.
In the filing, Icahn suggested the RJR Nabisco stockholders not adopt a rights plan, known as a "poison pill," for the company or any of its component companies.

He also said shareholders should attempt to work with members of the tobacco industry, the U.S. Congress, lawyers and the Clinton administration toward a global legislative settlement of tobacco litigation.

Icahn and his companies said they were weighing their next moves with respect to RJR Nabisco, including the feasibility of conducting a proxy contest, either at a special stockholder meeting or at the next annual meeting.
